Sani
 Versus
 The Sate Of Madhya Pradesh And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Shashank Upadhyay - Advocate for the applicant.
 Shri S.K. Gupta - Panel Lawyer for the respondent/State.
 None for the victim, despite service of notice.

Order 
This is second application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. for grant of regular bail relating to FIR No.457/2023, dated 13.12.2023, registered at Police Station-Palera,
District-Tikamgarh (M.P.) for commission of offence punishable under Section 363, 366, 376(2)(n),
120-B of IPC, Section 5/6 of POCSO Act.
Applicant is in detention since 27.12.2023.
Applicant's first bail application has been dismissed as withdrawn and not pressed vide order dated 15.03.2024, passed in M.Cr.C.No.8710/2024.
However, liberty was granted to renew the prayer for grant of bail after prosecutrix's evidence before the trial Court.

2 . As per the prosecution story, on 13.12.2023, 17 years and 7 months old prosecutrix's father lodged an FIR about missing of her youngest daughter who had left home for school for taking the examination.

When she did not came back and despite search she could not be traced, FIR was registered and after investigation, charge sheet has been filed for commission of the aforesaid NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:40485 2 MCRC-31469-2024 offences.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that applicant has not committed any offence.
He is innocent.
He has been falsely implicated.
Prosecutrix was a consenting party.
Therefore, no offence of rape/aggravated penetrative sexual assault is made out against the applicant.

Witnesses Sani vs The Sate Of Madhya Pradesh on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49934249/
1 are not appearing for tendering evidence.

entities.text: Sani vs The Sate Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On the aforesaid pretext it is prayed that applicant may be released on bail, pending the trial.

4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed the prayer for grant of bail to the applicant and has submitted that applicant is already a married person and despite that he took prosecutrix and committed rape/penetrative sexual assault upon her.

5 On a perusal of the statement of the prosecutrix and other material available on record, it is apparent that it is a case where a minor girl has been abused by a married man by taking her away from the home.

Therefore, having taken into consideration all the facts and circumstances of the case, but without expressing anything on the merits of the case, I am of the view that it is not a fit case for grant of bail at this stage.

6. Consequently, this second bail application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. filed on behalf of applicant - Sani is dismissed (DINESH KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE Jasleen Sani vs The Sate Of Madhya Pradesh on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49934249/
